synopsis: Residual safe distance is an explicit part of the stopping budget: ISO 21815-3:2023 includes detection, determination, action, machine stopping and final safe clearance; the reviewed 2022 draft defines safe distance as an authorised person's safe offset plus measurement error [f5911, f6198, f2420]. MOSH specifies stop gaps of 1.0–4.0 m at speeds of 10 km/h or less and 15 m ± 5 m above 10 km/h, whereas South Africa Regulation 8.10 and US 30 CFR 75.1732 provide no numeric stopping-margin value; the proposed US 3 ft distance was not adopted [f2610, f2611, f2626]. The booklet calculates remaining margin by subtracting perception, decision, action, predicted stopping distance and safe clearance from predicted path distance; its 40 t example at 15 km/h on a 10% downgrade with 1.0 s delay requires detection at least 9.5 m away for 1 m clearance, before sensor-error allowance [f6208, f13656]. Validation should measure stopping margin and minimum clearance in closed-loop runs, and tuning should impose a hard minimum-margin constraint rather than relying only on detector performance or collision/no-collision verdicts [f4812, f6961, f6982, f7373]. Intervention escalation should depend on remaining margin and its uncertainty rather than range alone, and operator-reaction detection must avoid standing down merely because controls move while the actual stopping margin continues collapsing [f6280, f6343, f13968].
